samples.question: The top of this image holds a thin gray key box containing two horizontal plates, one above the other; the vertical empty space between them is the reference aperture. Thin gray lines split the area below the key box into four panels side by side, counted from the left. Each panel contains two vertical posts, and the horizontal empty space between that panel's two posts is that panel's aperture. Every plate and post in the image is drawn with the same thickness. Exactly one panel has an aperture exactly as wide as the reference aperture is tall; every other panel's aperture differs from the reference by more than one bar thickness. Bar colour, post height, post placement, plate length, panel position and the amount of ink in a panel carry no information about the answer, and the matching aperture is not systematically the widest or the narrowest one. Which half of the panel strip contains the matching aperture, given that the first two panels form the left half and the last two form the right half? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.
